body_en: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after Trump intervenes

Nvidia ’s shares have surged by 31% at the start of trading following the news. The S+P 500 jumped 4.5% and is recovering nearly half of its brutal losses from last week, which was one of its worst since the 2008 financial crisis. Rallies for AI stocks had the Nasdaq composite up a market-leading 6.5%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1,117 points.
Here’s Trump ’s full social media post, in which he also called Jensen Huang “a Great Patriot and National Treasure”.

The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure. Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security. Congratulations to Jensen, the NVIDIA Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World!

这是特朗普完整的社交媒体帖子，其中他还称黄仁勋为“伟大的爱国者和国宝”。

NVIDIA 董事会做出了让黄仁勋重回首席执行官职位的正确决定。美国需要 Jensen 在 NVIDIA 的领导，以确保公司乃至美国经济的成功和繁荣。美国政府没有理由相信 Jensen 重返 NVIDIA 对国家安全构成任何风险。美国总检察长已确认，美国政府没有证据表明他有任何非法行为。就个人而言，我认识了詹森，他是一位伟大的爱国者和国宝。另外，NVIDIA 应继续对公司遵守美国出口管制的情况进行彻底的内部调查，以确保其履行保护美国国家安全的法律义务和爱国义务。向 NVIDIA 董事会 Jensen 以及美国人民以及全世界人民表示祝贺！

title_en: Trump urges justice department to speed up federal executions in dig at Gavin Newsom
title_zh: 特朗普敦促司法部加快联邦处决进程，挖掘加文·纽瑟姆的罪名
summary: President, in partisan speech, targeted California governor’s decision to commute death sentences of 548 prisoners Donald Trump on Monday urged the Department of Justice to speed up federal executions, in a partisan speech that targeted the California governor
summary_zh: 总统在党派演讲中针对加州州长对 548 名囚犯减刑的决定，唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 周一敦促德州政府
body_en: President, in partisan speech, targeted California governor’s decision to commute death sentences of 548 prisoners

Donald Trump on Monday urged the Department of Justice to speed up federal executions, in a partisan speech that targeted the California governor’s decision to spare the lives of all prisoners on death row in the state.

Speaking at the justice department , Trump assailed Gavin Newsom, a frequent Democratic critic who is considering a White House bid, and ordered the attorney general to expedite federal executions despite a recent outcry over a series of botched executions .
He also said he would sign a presidential directive ordering the department to seek the death penalty for child murderers, as well as rapists and human traffickers who kill their victims.
“Once juries have spoken, capital punishment will be swift and certain,” Trump told an audience in Washington.
Federal appeals court hands Trump way out of conviction in hush-money case

The death penalty has come under renewed scrutiny since September when Christa Pike , 50, became the first person to survive receiving doses of a drug during a lethal injection execution. Last week the execution in Texas of Reinaldo Dennes , 70, lasted more than an hour as staff struggled to find a suitable vein.

The US is increasingly isolated in its use of capital punishment: just 17 countries carried out executions in 2025, while 145 have abolished the death penalty in law or practice. Yet the US executed 47 people last year , the highest number since 2009.

Trump’s appetite for tough-on-crime rhetoric dates back to 1989, when he called for the restoration of the death penalty after five young Black and Latino men were wrongly accused in the Central Park jogger case.

Flanked by two 12.5ft aluminum statues from 1936, The Spirit of Justice and The Majesty of Law, Trump delivered Monday’s address on a stage in the great hall of the Robert F Kennedy Department of Justice building . He was joined by Todd Blanche, the attorney general, and Kash Patel, the FBI director, at an event attended by families of murder victims whose relatives were affected by Newsom’s mass commutation of death row inmates.

In his remarks, Trump described the governor’s decision to commute the death sentences of 548 prisoners – the largest clearing of any US death row in modern history – as “one of the most shocking acts of injustice our country has ever seen”.

He described the Democrat as a “terrible” governor and claimed that the commutations “should not be allowed to stand”, accusing him of granting clemency to some of “the most evil monsters on the face of the Earth”.

Trump added: “We come together to stand against the travesty and to wrap our arms around the families of victims who were so brutally betrayed by bad government and our political system. What these families have endured is beyond imagination.”

In graphic and gruesome terms, the president cited several notorious murder cases, including those of serial killer Charles Ng, who tortured and murdered at least 11 people, and Chester Turner, who killed 14 women in Los Angeles.

He invited relatives of some victims to speak, with several criticising Newsom’s decision. Sandy Friend , whose eight-year-old son Michael Lyons was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, challenged the governor to explain his decision. “Face me, Governor Newsom. Tell me Michael’s life doesn’t matter,” she said.

Blanche, Trump’s former personal defence lawyer, told the audience that the justice department was seeking the death penalty whenever appropriate. He said the justice department had sought the death penalty 49 times since Trump took office, compared with just once under Joe Biden.

Newsom announced earlier this month that he intended to commute all 548 death sentences in California to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole. The move does not release any prisoners, overturn convictions or remove restitution obligations, and most of the commutations require approval from the California supreme court.
Newsom has argued that capital punishment is morally wrong and inconsistent with California’s values, describing the death penalty system as arbitrary, unequal and vulnerable to wrongful convictions.
California has not carried out an execution since January 2006, although voters rejected proposals to abolish the death penalty in 2012 and 2016.
body_zh: 总统在党派演讲中针对加州州长为 548 名囚犯减刑的决定
唐纳德·特朗普周一在一场党派演讲中敦促司法部加快联邦处决速度，演讲针对的是加州州长饶恕该州所有死囚的决定。
特朗普在司法部发表讲话，攻击了正在考虑入主白宫的经常批评民主党的加文·纽瑟姆(Gavin Newsom)，并命令司法部长加快联邦处决，尽管最近对一系列拙劣的处决引发了强烈抗议。
他还表示，他将签署一项总统指令，命令该部门对杀害儿童的凶手以及杀害受害者的强奸犯和人口贩运者寻求死刑。
特朗普在华盛顿对观众说：“一旦陪审团发表意见，死刑将是迅速且确定的。”
联邦上诉法院让特朗普免于封口费案定罪
自9月份以来，死刑受到了新的审查，当时50岁的克里斯塔·派克(Christa Pike)成为第一个在注射死刑期间接受药物而幸存的人。上周，德克萨斯州 70 岁的雷纳尔多·丹尼斯 (Reinaldo Dennes) 的处决持续了一个多小时，工作人员努力寻找合适的静脉。
美国在使用死刑方面日益孤立：只有17个国家在2025年执行了死刑，而145个国家在法律或实践中废除了死刑。然而，美国去年处决了 47 人，这是自 2009 年以来的最高数字。
特朗普对严厉打击犯罪言论的兴趣可以追溯到 1989 年，当时五名年轻的黑人和拉丁裔男子在中央公园慢跑者案中受到错误指控，当时他呼吁恢复死刑。
周一，特朗​​普在罗伯特·F·肯尼迪司法部大楼大厅的舞台上发表讲话，两侧是 1936 年的两座 12.5 英尺高的铝制雕像“正义精神”和“法律陛下”。司法部长托德·布兰奇和联邦调查局局长卡什·帕特尔与他一起参加了一场由谋杀受害者家属参加的活动，这些受害者的亲属受到纽瑟姆对死囚大规模减刑的影响。
特朗普在讲话中称，州长为 548 名囚犯减刑的决定——这是美国现代历史上对死囚牢房最大规模的清理——是“我们国家所见过的最令人震惊的不公正行为之一”。
他形容这位民主党人是一位“可怕的”州长，并声称减刑“不应该继续存在”，指责他对一些“地球上最邪恶的怪物”给予宽大处理。
特朗普补充道：“我们团结起来反对这种嘲讽，并拥抱那些被糟糕的政府和我们的政治制度残酷背叛的受害者家属。这些家庭所承受的苦难是超乎想象的。”
总统用生动而可怕的措辞列举了几起臭名昭著的谋杀案，其中包括折磨和谋杀至少 11 人的连环杀手查尔斯·吴 (Charles Ng) 的案件，以及在洛杉矶杀害 14 名妇女的切斯特·特纳 (Chester Turner) 的案件。
他邀请一些受害者的亲属发表讲话，其中一些人批评了纽瑟姆的决定。桑迪·弗兰德 (Sandy Friend) 八岁的儿子迈克尔·莱昂斯 (Michael Lyons) 遭到绑架、酷刑和谋杀，他要求州长解释他的决定。 “面对我，纽瑟姆州长。告诉我迈克尔的生命并不重要，”她说。
特朗普的前私人辩护律师布兰奇告诉观众，司法部正在寻求在适当的时候判处死刑。他说，自特朗普上任以来，司法部已49次寻求死刑，而乔·拜登执政期间仅一次。
纽瑟姆本月早些时候宣布，他打算将加州所有 548 名死刑判决减为终身监禁，且不得假释。此举不会释放任何囚犯、推翻定罪或取消归还义务，而且大部分减刑都需要加州最高法院的批准。
纽瑟姆认为，死刑在道德上是错误的，也不符合加州的价值观，他认为死刑制度是任意的、不平等的，而且很容易被错误定罪。
尽管选民在2012年和2016年拒绝了废除死刑的提议，但加州自2006年1月以来就没有执行过死刑。

title_en: Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
title_zh: 特朗普命令联邦承包商在回应国会之前先与白宫核实
summary: President Trump is directing federal contractors to consult the White House about inquiries from Congress and to withhold any communications that his administration considers privileged.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统指示联邦承包商就国会的询问向白宫咨询，并隐瞒他的任何信息。
body_en: Trump moves to limit contractors contact with Congress : NPR

Trump moves to limit contractors contact with Congress President Trump is directing federal contractors to consult the White House about inquiries from Congress and to withhold any communications that his administration considers privileged.
President Trump speaks at a news conference in the James Brady Press Briefing Room of the White House, Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, in Washington. Jacquelyn Martin/AP hide caption

NEW YORK (AP) — President Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged, according to a new executive order .

The companies must also coordinate with the White House and U.S. agencies on "appropriate responses" to any such requests, the order issued late Friday says. If they fail to comply, the White House warns their contracts could be terminated and their future work with the federal government suspended.

The order is the Republican administration's latest effort to resist what are expected to be wide-ranging and aggressive oversight efforts from Democrats when they take over Congress in January. Democrats have made government contracts one of their top investigative targets , noting that federal money has been flowing to companies linked with Trump's family, particularly at the Pentagon.

White House officials have already begun taking steps to exert more control over how agencies and officials respond to congressional requests, anticipating there will be a flood of investigations initiated by Democrats.

Trump's counsel, Will Scharf, told federal agencies on Monday that they must seek approval from his office and the White House's Office of Legislative Affairs before agreeing to appear before Congress. Scharf also suggested in a recent letter to Rep. Robert Garcia of California, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, that some congressional investigations may amount to "blatant criminality."

Garcia sent letters this week directing members of Trump's family and top administration officials to preserve documents. Scharf sought to dismiss the requests, noting in a letter to Democratic lawmakers that they are not yet in the majority and cannot compel compliance.

Responding to the new executive order, Garcia said it was part of the administration's "blatant attack on Congress' constitutional right to conduct oversight." He said that despite efforts to impede investigations, "we're just getting started."

In a fact sheet , the White House framed the new requirements as "protecting executive privileges from congressional overreach," arguing that some congressional leaders have tried to intrude on executive branch privileges by "harassing private companies that contract with the federal government."

Presidents of both parties have long used executive privilege to resist congressional inquiries, but the claims can set up messy, protracted legal fights as parties dispute whether it applies. Executive privilege allows the president to keep information from the courts, Congress and the public to protect the confidentiality of White House deliberations, but the protection is far from absolute.
The latest executive order applies to all contractors and subcontractors, a universe of tens of thousands of businesses.

body_zh: 特朗普采取行动限制承包商与国会的接触：NPR
特朗普采取行动限制承包商与国会的接触特朗普总统正在指示联邦承包商就国会的询问向白宫咨询，并保留其政府认为有特权的任何通信。
特朗普总统于 2026 年 11 月 20 日星期五在华盛顿白宫詹姆斯·布雷迪新闻发布会室举行的新闻发布会上发表讲话。杰奎琳·马丁/美联社隐藏标题栏
纽约（美联社）——根据一项新的行政命令，唐纳德·特朗普总统指示联邦承包商和分包商就国会提出的质询与他的政府进行磋商，并扣留任何白宫认为有特权的通信。
周五晚些时候发布的命令称，这些公司还必须与白宫和美国机构协调，对任何此类请求做出“适当回应”。如果他们不遵守规定，白宫警告他们的合同可能会被终止，并且他们未来与联邦政府的合作可能会暂停。
该命令是共和党政府为抵制民主党在一月份接管国会时预计将采取的广泛而积极的监督措施而采取的最新举措。民主党人已将政府合同作为其首要调查目标之一，并指出联邦资金一直流向与特朗普家族有联系的公司，尤其是五角大楼。
白宫官员已经开始采取措施，对各机构和官员如何回应国会要求施加更多控制，预计民主党将发起大量调查。
特朗普的律师威尔·沙夫周一告诉联邦机构，他们必须获得特朗普办公室和白宫立法事务办公室的批准，然后才能同意出席国会会议。沙夫还在最近给众议院监督委员会民主党领袖、加州众议员罗伯特·加西亚的一封信中表示，一些国会调查可能构成“公然犯罪”。
加西亚本周致函特朗普家族成员和高级政府官员保存文件。沙夫试图驳回这些要求，并在给民主党议员的一封信中指出，他们尚未占多数，无法强迫他们遵守。
加西亚在回应新的行政命令时表示，这是政府“公然攻击国会监督权的宪法权利”的一部分。他说，尽管有人努力阻止调查，但“我们才刚刚开始”。
在一份情况说明书中，白宫将新要求描述为“保护行政特权免遭国会越权”，并认为一些国会领导人试图通过“骚扰与联邦政府签订合同的私营公司”来侵犯行政部门的特权。
两党总统长期以来一直利用行政特权来抵制国会调查，但由于双方对其是否适用存在争议，这些主张可能会引发混乱、旷日持久的法律斗争。行政特权允许总统向法院、国会和公众保留信息，以保护白宫审议的机密性，但这种保护远非绝对。
最新的行政命令适用于所有承包商和分包商，涵盖数以万计的企业。

title_en: Trump targets Newsom and Democrats in Justice Department speech focused on violent crime
title_zh: 特朗普在司法部针对暴力犯罪的演讲中针对纽瑟姆和民主党人
summary: President Donald Trump has condemned California Governor Gavin Newsom's decision to commute hundreds of death sentences
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统谴责加州州长加文·纽瑟姆为数百名死刑减刑的决定
body_en: President Donald Trump has condemned California Governor Gavin Newsom's decision to commute hundreds of death sentences

WASHINGTON -- President Donald Trump condemned California Gov. Gavin Newsom’s decision to commute hundreds of death sentences in the state, using a Justice Department visit to sharply chastise an outspoken Democratic critic who is considering his own bid for the White House.

The speech offered the president a platform to showcase what he said was his administration's success in combating violent crime, a favored Trump topic he has repeatedly invoked to rally his Republican base. But the address, Trump's second at the department in less than two years , veered openly into partisan politics as the president lambasted both a governor with whom he has openly feuded and a Democratic Party he depicted as soft-on-crime and part of a “radical left.”

“For years now, we have watched the radical left commit one betrayal of justice and safety after another,” Trump said in a speech that was also interspersed with first-person accounts from relatives of victims of crimes affected by Newsom's clemency who criticized the commutations.

Newsom has said the announcement this month to commute the sentences of more than 500 inmates to punishments of life in prison without parole was among the most difficult choices of his career because it will surface painful memories for crime victims’ families. The state’s Supreme Court would be required to approve the majority of those commutations.

“I won’t take lectures on accountability from a president who has used the pardon power to help wealthy friends and business associates avoid accountability while victims are left fighting to recover what was stolen from them. Justice should be about the people we serve, not the political interests of the people in power,” Newsom said in a statement about Trump's speech.

Asked at an event Monday why he didn't take the death penalty reveal to the ballot, Newsom said he had the “constitutional right” to do what he did. He added: “I may be the first to have received the kind of response from the sitting president of the United States at the Department of Justice with the FBI director — talk about weaponization.”
The speech marked the latest tussle between Trump and Newsom.

In June, Newsom accused the Justice Department of launching a politically motivated investigation into him and his wife, which his office said was focused on “increasingly personal matters involving the governor’s family and professional network.” He has denied any wrongdoing. The president has repeatedly gone after the heavily Democratic California during his second term and the state has pushed back by suing the federal government dozens of times.

The president's address unfolded against the backdrop of sweeping Republican losses in this month’s midterm elections , which gave Democrats control of the House and Senate. The development tees up possible congressional inquiries into everything from the mass firings of federal agents and prosecutors by the Trump administration Justice Department to a series of politically charged investigations into Trump adversaries that have been rejected by grand juries and judges alike.

Trump was introduced by Attorney General Todd Blanche , his former personal defense lawyer who has been unapologetic in his view that the Justice Department as an executive branch agency is an extension of the White House and that the president is free to exert his will over the institution. He said Monday that the Justice Department in the Trump administration was seeking the death penalty whenever appropriate.

“I want to take just a moment and tell every law enforcement member watching or here in this room that we have your back, that President Trump has your back, and he will always have your back,” Blanche said.

Trump has long sought to position himself as a tough-on-crime president who staunchly backs law enforcement. He has taken credit for dropping violent crime rates that experts say have been declining since 2022.

"Our opponents seek an America that empowers the most violent and dangerous elements and celebrates deviancy and enables dysfunction and demands empathy for serial killers and criminals, while hardworking citizens are treated with hatred and scorn and contempt,” Trump said Monday. “In the Trump administration, we believe in the exact opposite.”

As with last year’s speech, Monday’s remarks were delivered inside the ceremonial Great Hall of the Justice Department headquarters, a building whose exterior in the last year was decorated with a massive banner of Trump’s face in a physical demonstration of the president’s sway over the agency.

Trump's March 2025 address was meant to rally support for his administration’s policies on violent crime, drugs and illegal immigration but became a forum for a litany of complaints about the criminal cases Trump faced during Democratic President Joe Biden’s administration — when prosecutors charged him with hoarding classified documents at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Palm Beach, Florida, and with conspiring to overturn his 2020 election loss to Biden — and to vow retribution for what he described as the “lies and abuses that have occurred within these walls.”
body_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统谴责加州州长加文·纽瑟姆为数百名死刑减刑的决定
华盛顿——唐纳德·特朗普总统谴责加州州长加文·纽瑟姆对该州数百名死刑犯减刑的决定，并利用司法部的访问严厉惩罚了一位正在考虑入主白宫的直言不讳的民主党批评者。
这次演讲为总统提供了一个平台，展示他所说的政府在打击暴力犯罪方面所取得的成功，这是特朗普最喜欢的话题，他曾多次援引这一话题来团结他的共和党基础。但特朗普在不到两年的时间里在该部门发表的第二次讲话，公开地转向了党派政治，总统痛斥了一位与他公开不和的州长，以及他将民主党描绘成对犯罪温和、属于“激进左翼”的民主党。
特朗普在一次演讲中表示，“多年来，我们看到激进左派一次又一次背叛正义和安全。”演讲中还穿插了受纽瑟姆宽大处理影响的犯罪受害者亲属的第一人称叙述，他们对减刑提出了批评。
纽瑟姆表示，本月宣布将 500 多名囚犯的刑期减为终身监禁且不得假释，这是他职业生涯中最困难的选择之一，因为这将给犯罪受害者家属带来痛苦的记忆。其中大部分减刑必须得到该州最高法院的批准。
纽瑟姆在一份有关特朗普演讲的声明中表示：“我不会听一位总统关于问责制的讲座，他利用赦免权帮助富有的朋友和商业伙伴逃避责任，而受害者却在为追回被盗的东西而奋斗。正义应该是关于我们所服务的人民​​，而不是当权者的政治利益。”
纽瑟姆在周一的一次活动中被问及为何不将死刑公布纳入投票时表示，他有“宪法权利”去做他所做的事情。他补充道：“我可能是第一个收到美国司法部现任总统与联邦调查局局长的此类回应的人——谈论武器化。”
这次演讲标志着特朗普和纽瑟姆之间的最新争执。
今年六月，纽瑟姆指责司法部对他和他的妻子发起了出于政治动机的调查，他的办公室表示，调查的重点是“越来越多涉及州长家庭和专业网络的个人事务”。他否认有任何不当行为。总统在第二个任期内多次针对民主党占主导地位的加州，而该州则多次起诉联邦政府进行反击。
总统的讲话是在共和党在本月中期选举中惨败的背景下发表的，这次中期选举让民主党控制了参众两院。这一事态发展为国会可能对一切问题进行调查，从特朗普政府司法部大规模解雇联邦特工和检察官，到对特朗普对手进行的一系列政治调查，但这些调查均被大陪审团和法官拒绝。
特朗普是由他的前私人辩护律师、司法部长托德·布兰奇(Todd Blanche)介绍的。布兰奇一直毫无歉意地认为，司法部作为行政部门是白宫的延伸，总统可以自由地对该机构行使自己的意愿。他周一表示，特朗普政府司法部正在寻求在适当的时候判处死刑。
布兰奇说：“我想花一点时间告诉每一位正在观看或在座的执法人员，我们支持你，特朗普总统支持你，他将永远支持你。”

title_en: Federal court clears way for army to detonate bomb-making chemicals in Iowa
title_zh: 联邦法院为军队在爱荷华州引爆炸弹化学品扫清道路
summary: Trump, on social media, tried to push responsibility of ‘any and all death or destruction’ on Democratic governor-elect The US army can proceed with detonating several tons of degraded bomb-making chemicals in Iowa, a federal appeals court ruled on Monday. The
summary_zh: 特朗普在社交媒体上试图将“任何和所有死亡或破坏”的责任推给民主党当选州长美国军队可以继续进行
body_en: Trump, on social media, tried to push responsibility of ‘any and all death or destruction’ on Democratic governor-elect

The US army can proceed with detonating several tons of degraded bomb-making chemicals in Iowa , a federal appeals court ruled on Monday. The order came after a day of uncertainty that saw Donald Trump attempt to foist responsibility “for any and all death or destruction” on Iowa’s Democratic governor-elect Rob Sands.

The detonation of 68 barrels containing nearly 9,500lb of lead azide was initially planned for Friday, but the army has since changed the date three times after an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects.

In a social media post hours before the eighth circuit panel ruling, Trump wrote that he preferred to take care of the volatile material as soon as possible and that a controlled detonation would be much safer, but that he was “making this decision fully subject to the incoming Governor Elect, Rob Sand, agreeing to the operation”.

“If he or the Courts do not agree, we will have no choice but to not proceed with the controlled removal of these hazardous materials, and be forced to hold the incoming Governor responsible for any and all death or destruction caused by this very unfortunate, and longterm, situation,” Trump added.

Sand, who does not take office until January, called for more transparency from the federal government in a statement on Monday. “Everyday Iowans are entitled to know how Middletown came to this situation, and learn why the administration believes this is the best path forward,” he wrote on social media, noting that he has been receiving briefings on the operation from the administration. “I’ve asked the federal government to share that information with the public as soon as possible.”

Nearly 400 people live in Middletown, a small town in south-eastern Iowa, where the plant is situated. The army has warned that the blast could release a plume of toxic lead dust extending up to 100 miles northeast, possibly reaching cities such as Wapello and New Boston, Illinois.
On Friday, current Iowa governor Kim Reynolds, a Republican, activated the state emergency management office, and the state created a website for information about the detonation.

Republican Chuck Grassley, the long-serving Iowa senator, echoed Sand’s call for “increased communication and transparency to the public” but said he supported “a controlled, safe removal” over “a spontaneous catastrophe”.

In his social media post, Trump blamed the existence of the lead azide barrels at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on the Obama administration, which he said “improperly stored a vast number of explosives” there in 2009.

According to the Des Moines Register , the filing said that the lead azide, an explosive made of lead and nitrogen used primarily in detonators and blasting caps, has been left vulnerable to temperature swings because the blast doors to bunkers containing the compound had been removed and could not be replaced.

In a court filing, the US Department of Justice notified the appeals court that the army would invoke an emergency exception to go ahead with the explosion. But that was challenged in court by the Iowa Environmental Council and the Sierra Club’s Iowa chapter, arguing that the Environmental Protection Agency had skipped necessary permitting steps.

The court then put an administrative stay on the permit so that it could review the emergency motion. In response, the government said there is “an immediate risk” that the lead will explode as temperatures drop below 30 degrees in the upcoming days.
On Monday, a three-judge panel of the eighth circuit court of appeals said the EPA adequately incorporated safeguards in an emergency permit to minimize the dispersal of dust.

Officials acknowledge that lead is toxic and have recommended that people stay indoors whenever the detonation happens and clean off outdoor surfaces with water afterward to limit exposure to any lead particles.

The leaders of states bordering Iowa have expressed concern about the detonation. Mike Kehoe, the Missouri Republican governor, said state agencies are working to establish additional monitoring of air and water quality, public health and agriculture resources, but emphasized “this is a federal operation” and “the states of Iowa, Missouri and Illinois do not have a say on when this is conducted”.
Tammy Baldwin, the Wisconsin Democratic governor, sent a letter on Monday to Adam Telle, the army secretary, expressing “alarm and disapproval” over the handling of the lead azide.
The army initially scheduled the demolition for 20 November, but over the weekend moved it to allow for “more optimal weather conditions and all mitigation measures to be emplaced”.

Environmentalists sued last week in an effort to stop the detonation, winning a stay from the appeals court pending a decision on the validity of an emergency permit approved by the US Environmental Protection Agency that cleared the way for the operation.
body_zh: 特朗普在社交媒体上试图将“任何和所有死亡或破坏”的责任推给民主党当选州长
联邦上诉法院周一裁定，美国军队可以在爱荷华州继续引爆数吨降解的炸弹制造化学品。该命令是在一天的不确定性之后发布的，唐纳德·特朗普试图将“所有死亡或破坏”的责任强加给爱荷华州民主党当选州长罗布·桑兹。
最初计划于周五引爆 68 个装有近 9,500 磅叠氮化铅的桶，但由于公众对潜在的健康和环境影响表示担忧，军队已三度更改日期。
在第八巡回小组裁决前几个小时，特朗普在社交媒体上发帖写道，他更愿意尽快处理掉挥发性物质，受控爆炸会安全得多，但他“做出这一决定完全取决于即将上任的州长罗布·桑德是否同意此次行动”。
特朗普补充说：“如果他或法院不同意，我们将别无选择，只能不继续有控制地清除这些危险材料，并被迫让即将上任的州长对这种非常不幸的长期情况造成的任何和所有死亡或破坏负责。”
桑德要到一月份才上任，他在周一的一份声明中呼吁联邦政府提高透明度。他在社交媒体上写道：“爱荷华州人民每天都有权了解米德尔敦是如何陷入这种境地的，并了解为什么政府认为这是最好的前进道路。”他指出，他一直在收到政府有关此次行动的简报。 “我已要求联邦政府尽快与公众分享这些信息。”
该工厂所在的爱荷华州东南部小镇米德尔敦有近 400 人居住。军方警告说，爆炸可能会释放出有毒的铅尘，向东北延伸100英里，可能到达伊利诺伊州瓦佩洛和新波士顿等城市。
周五，现任爱荷华州州长、共和党人金·雷诺兹启动了州紧急事务管理办公室，该州还创建了一个网站来提供有关爆炸的信息。
长期任职的爱荷华州参议员、共和党人查克·格拉斯利(Chuck Grassley)回应了桑德关于“加强与公众的沟通和透明度”的呼吁，但表示他支持“可控、安全的驱逐”，而不是“自发的灾难”。
特朗普在社交媒体帖子中将爱荷华州陆军弹药厂叠氮化铅桶的存在归咎于奥巴马政府，他称奥巴马政府于2009年在那里“不当储存了大量爆炸物”。
据《得梅因纪事报》报道，文件称，叠氮化铅是一种由铅和氮气制成的炸药，主要用于雷管和雷管，它很容易受到温度波动的影响，因为含有该化合物的掩体的防爆门已被拆除且无法更换。
在一份法庭文件中，美国司法部通知上诉法院，军队将援引紧急例外情况继续进行爆炸。但这一说法在法庭上受到爱荷华州环境委员会和塞拉俱乐部爱荷华州分会的质疑，认为环境保护局跳过了必要的许可步骤。
随后，法院对许可证进行了行政暂缓，以便可以审查紧急动议。作为回应，政府表示，随着未来几天气温降至 30 度以下，铅存在“直接风险”。
周一，第八巡回上诉法院的三名法官组成的小组表示，环保局在紧急许可证中充分纳入了保障措施，以尽量减少灰尘的扩散。
官员们承认铅有毒，并建议人们在爆炸发生时呆在室内，然后用水清洁室外表面，以限制接触任何铅颗粒。
与爱荷华州接壤的各州领导人对爆炸表示担忧。密苏里州共和党州长迈克·基霍表示，各州机构正在努力对空气和水质、公共卫生和农业资源进行额外的监测，但强调“这是一项联邦行动”，“爱荷华州、密苏里州和伊利诺伊州对何时进行这一行动没有发言权”。
威斯康星州民主党州长塔米·鲍德温 (Tammy Baldwin) 周一致信陆军部长亚当·特尔 (Adam Telle)，对叠氮化铅的处理表示“震惊和不满”。
陆军最初计划于 11 月 20 日进行拆除工作，但在周末推迟了时间，以允许“更佳的天气条件和采取所有缓解措施”。
环保人士上周提起诉讼，试图阻止爆炸，并赢得了上诉法院的暂缓执行，等待美国环境保护署批准的紧急许可证的有效性决定，该许可证为这次行动扫清了道路。

title_en: US adds Megaspeed, AI firm at center of Nvidia scandal, to trade blacklist
title_zh: 美国将英伟达丑闻中心的人工智能公司Megaspeed列入交易黑名单
summary: Singapore-based company entangled in scandal over alleged spy Alice Huang’s affair with Jensen Huang The US commerce department published an official notice on Monday adding the Singapore-based company Megaspeed, and its subsidiaries in Thailand and Malaysia,
summary_zh: 新加坡公司卷入涉嫌间谍黄仁勋与黄仁勋的风流丑闻 美国商务部发布官方声明
body_en: Singapore-based company entangled in scandal over alleged spy Alice Huang’s affair with Jensen Huang
The US commerce department published an official notice on Monday adding the Singapore-based company Megaspeed, and its subsidiaries in Thailand and Malaysia, to a trade blacklist.
Republican lawmakers break with Trump over alleged Nvidia chip smuggling after Jensen Huang’s reinstatement – live

Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner which has been under investigation by US authorities since 2024 over whether it diverted AI chips to China, will now need approval from the commerce department to obtain US exports, which is likely to be denied.

The expected addition of the company follows revelations that the recently reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a ⁠relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and Megaspeed’s controlling shareholder, who is reportedly alleged to be a ⁠spy for Beijing. China has said the spy accusations are “groundless”.
Lawrence Wong, Singapore’s prime minister, says the country is conducting its own investigation into Megaspeed; however, it isn’t involved in the US inquiry.

“With regards to Jensen Huang’s role, we are not involved in those investigations; it’s for the American government to decide, and we leave them to make those investigations and judgments,” Wong said in a Monday evening news conference. “If there are companies that are caught breaching our laws, we will certainly take very firm enforcement actions. So it’s on that basis that we were investigating Megaspeed.”
Singapore had previously investigated Alice Huang, but found no basis for prosecution, Wong said.
“The Department of Commerce still needs to explain to Congress why this took so long,” Senator Pete Ricketts, a Nebraska Republican, said in a social media post.

The New York Times reported on Monday that Alice Huang “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year while she was carrying out a secret affair with Jensen Huang, according to multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports that describe the encounters”.
The US justice department is investigating whether Megaspeed violated US export controls by shipping Nvidia chips to China.
Megaspeed did not immediately return a request for comment. A week ago, the company issued a statement saying it conducts legitimate and lawful business, including complying with US export controls.
It also said Alice Huang officially left Megaspeed in August 2025.
Nvidia has said it recently formed an export control committee to oversee trade compliance and national security risks.

As Semafor notes, the US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, has been under pressure to act since the news of Jensen Huang’s relationship with the former reporter for Chinese state television who became a director at Singapore-based Megaspeed in 2023 became public.

The US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, said earlier this month that his agency along with the Pentagon, the state department and the US trade representative’s office had all wanted Megaspeed on the blacklist “for months” but that “Commerce holds the pen”.
After the news broke, treasury secretary Scott Bessent publicly complained that the commerce department had not yet placed the company on its entity list.

He also called out Nvidia. “The real story here should be: did Nvidia know their client and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?” Bessent told CNBC’s Squawk Box program.

The US justice department and commerce department issued a joint statement last week saying they would “bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred”.
body_zh: 总部位于新加坡的公司因涉嫌间谍爱丽丝黄与黄仁勋的风流韵事而卷入丑闻
美国商务部周一发布正式通知，将新加坡公司 Megaspeed 及其在泰国和马来西亚的子公司列入贸易黑名单。
黄仁勋复职后，共和党议员就涉嫌英伟达芯片走私问题与特朗普决裂 – 直播
Nvidia 的合作伙伴 Megaspeed 自 2024 年以来一直因是否将人工智能芯片转移到中国而受到美国当局的调查，现在需要获得商务部的批准才能获得美国出口，而这一批准很可能会被拒绝。
预计该公司的加入是在最近重新上任的 Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 与中国女商人、Megaspeed 控股股东 Alice Huang 有关系的消息曝光后进行的，据报道，后者被指控为北京间谍。中国表示，间谍指控“毫无根据”。
新加坡总理黄循财表示，该国正在对 Megaspeed 进行自己的调查；不过，它并未参与美国的调查。
“至于黄仁勋的角色，我们不参与这些调查；这是由美国政府决定的，我们让他们做出这些调查和判断，”黄在周一晚间的新闻发布会上表示。 “如果有公司被发现违反我们的法律，我们肯定会采取非常严厉的执法行动。因此，我们正是在此基础上对 Megaspeed 进行了调查。”
黄说，新加坡此前曾对黄爱丽进行过调查，但没有发现起诉的依据。
“商务部仍然需要向国会解释为什么花了这么长时间，”内布拉斯加州共和党参议员皮特·里基茨(Pete Ricketts)在社交媒体帖子中表示。
《纽约时报》周一报道称，据多位了解美国情报报告的人士透露，爱丽丝·黄“在与黄仁勋进行秘密恋情期间，与中国最高间谍机构的一名官员保持了一年多的联系”。
美国司法部正在调查 Megaspeed 将 Nvidia 芯片运往中国是否违反了美国出口管制。
Megaspeed 没有立即回复置评请求。一周前，该公司发表声明称其开展合法合法业务，包括遵守美国出口管制。
它还表示，Alice Huang 已于 2025 年 8 月正式离开 Megaspeed。
英伟达表示，它最近成立了一个出口管制委员会，以监督贸易合规性和国家安全风险。
正如 Semafor 指出的那样，自从黄仁勋与中国国家电视台前记者、2023 年成为新加坡 Megaspeed 董事的关系的消息曝光以来，美国商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克 (Howard Lutnick) 一直面临着采取行动的压力。
美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特本月早些时候表示，他的机构以及五角大楼、国务院和美国贸易代表办公室“几个月来”都希望将 Megaspeed 列入黑名单，但“商务部握有权力”。
消息传出后，财政部长斯科特·贝森特公开抱怨商务部尚未将该公司列入实体名单。
他还点名了英伟达。 “这里真正的故事应该是：英伟达是否了解他们的客户，英伟达是否做出了强有力的努力来确保不存在泄密，以及他们是否将产品出售给明显是通过空壳公司？”贝森特告诉 CNBC 的 Squawk Box 节目。
美国司法部和商务部上周发表联合声明，称他们将“对 Megaspeed 可能发生的任何犯罪行为采取全面法律制裁”。

title_en: Trump uses backdrop of DOJ to bash Gavin Newsom on death row commutations
title_zh: 特朗普利用司法部的背景抨击加文·纽瑟姆的死囚减刑
summary: President Donald Trump gave his speech at the Justice Department headquarters — a rarity for a president — and invited victims’ family members to speak onstage.
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统在司法部总部发表讲话——这对总统来说是罕见的——并邀请受害者家属发表讲话
body_en: President Trump slams Calif. Gov. Newsom for commuting death sentences for more than 500 inmates

President Donald Trump on Monday delivered remarks at the Justice Department’s headquarters in Washington, denouncing Democratic California Gov. Gavin Newsom’s plan for commuting the death sentences of more than 500 convicted murderers.

It is rare for a president to speak at the Justice Department. Trump last did so in March 2025, when he called for jailing his perceived political foes. This time, he took swipes at Newsom , a potential 2028 presidential contender, whom he called a “terrible” governor.

“He stood with the murderers and the child slayers, but today we say the American people stand with you. We stand with you. We’re not going to let this happen,” Trump said, without elaborating on how his administration could intervene.
The death row sentences being commuted by Newsom all stem from state cases.

Trump also announced several new executive actions, including a presidential directive that he said ordered the DOJ to seek the death penalty for “child murderers, as well as rapists and human traffickers who kill their victims.” He added that the order would direct the attorney general to expedite the execution of federal death row inmates.

The president brought relatives of several victims onstage, who at times became emotional when describing how their loved ones had died. Some who spoke were the parents of victims whose killings made national news for years and sparked changes to the law.

Marc Klaas, whose 12-year-old daughter Polly was abducted from her home in Petaluma in 1993 before being killed, said he was “outraged” by Newsom’s actions. Actress Winona Ryder had offered a $200,000 reward for information at the time Polly went missing. The man convicted in her death, Richard Allen Davis, had a record and was previously released from prison — his conviction helped lead to California’s “three strikes” law that increased prison sentences for repeat offenders.
Another speaker, Sandy Friend, whose 8-year-old son Michael Lyons was killed by Robert Boyd Rhodes, asked Newsom to “face” her as she described her son’s death.

“His most feared thing was the dark. That night, Michael learned that the boogeyman was real. Mikey was raped, sodomized and tortured for 10 hours, from the very first inflicted stab wound to the last,” Friend said, choking up at one point while adding, “Sorry, this is so very hard.”
“Governor Newsom erased that with the swipe of a pen, without notifying the families,” Friend said of Rhodes’ death sentence.
Newsom responded to the DOJ event in a video message on social media , accusing the president of “selling” pardons and benefiting his associates.

“To the families standing with him today, your grief is real. That’s why every person, every person on California’s former death row will die in prison. No one walks out. Donald Trump’s criminals, they walk out,” Newsom said.

“A Justice Department that prosecutes his enemies and pardons himself and his friends — that’s not law enforcement. That’s a protection racket,” the governor added. He previously said, in announcing his plan, that “state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values.”

Trump wrapped up the somber event by shaking hands with the victims’ family members, some of whom had been in tears only minutes before. But the tone quickly shifted when his campaign anthem — the upbeat “YMCA” — played as he left the stage.

Newsom and Trump’s back-and-forth comes amid a series of botched executions across the country. Last week prison staffers in Texas struggled to find a vein on Reinaldo Dennes , resulting in an execution that lasted over an hour as Dennes cried out in pain. And in September, Christa Pike , the sole woman on Tennessee’s death row, became the first person to survive a lethal injection. She was placed on a ventilator and regained consciousness days later.
Support for the death penalty in the U.S. has generally been declining since a high of 80% in 1994, but Americans have complicated feelings about capital punishment.

A Gallup poll this month found that 49% of U.S. adults favored the death penalty for those convicted of murder, with 45% opposed. But a Pew Research Center survey in August found that 66% of Americans were in favor of the death penalty for those convicted of murder, though 59% said the death penalty was not a crime deterrent. There is also a partisan gap, with Democrats increasingly opposing the death penalty.
Raquel Coronell Uribe is a politics reporter for NBC News.
body_zh: 特朗普总统猛烈抨击加州州长纽瑟姆为 500 多名囚犯减刑
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周一在华盛顿司法部总部发表讲话，谴责民主党加州州长加文·纽瑟姆为 500 多名被定罪的杀人犯减刑的计划。
总统在司法部发表讲话是很少见的。特朗普上次这样做是在 2025 年 3 月，当时他呼吁监禁他所认为的政治敌人。这一次，他猛烈抨击了 2028 年总统候选人的潜在候选人纽森，称他是一位“可怕的”州长。
“他与凶手和儿童杀手站在一起，但今天我们说美国人民与你们站在一起。我们与你们站在一起。我们不会让这种情况发生，”特朗普说道，但没有详细说明他的政府将如何进行干预。
纽瑟姆减刑的死囚全部来自州案件。
特朗普还宣布了几项新的行政行动，其中包括一项总统指令，他称该指令命令司法部寻求对“儿童谋杀犯以及杀害受害者的强奸犯和人口贩运者”判处死刑。他补充说，该命令将指示司法部长加快处决联邦死囚。
总统将几名遇难者的亲属带到了台上，他们在描述亲人的死因时有时会情绪激动。一些发言者是受害者的父母，他们的杀戮多年来一直成为全国新闻，并引发了法律的修改。

马克·克拉斯 (Marc Klaas) 12 岁的女儿波莉 (Polly) 于 1993 年在佩塔卢马 (Petaluma) 的家中被绑架，随后被杀害。马克·克拉斯 (Marc Klaas) 表示，他对纽瑟姆的行为感到“愤怒”。波莉失踪时，女演员薇诺娜·瑞德悬赏 20 万美元寻找信息。因她的死亡而被定罪的男子理查德·艾伦·戴维斯(Richard Allen Davis)有前科，此前已出狱——他的定罪帮助加州制定了“三振”法，增加了对累犯的刑期。
另一位发言人桑迪·弗兰德 (Sandy Friend) 8 岁的儿子迈克尔·里昂斯 (Michael Lyons) 被罗伯特·博伊德·罗兹 (Robert Boyd Rhodes) 杀害，他要求纽瑟姆在描述儿子之死时“面对”她。
“他最害怕的事情就是黑暗。那天晚上，迈克尔得知那个妖怪是真实的。米奇被强奸、鸡奸和折磨了 10 个小时，从第一次刺伤到最后一次，”弗兰德说，他一度哽咽，同时补充道，“抱歉，这太难了。”
“纽瑟姆州长在没有通知家人的情况下，大笔一挥就将其删除了，”弗兰特谈到罗德的死刑判决时说道。
纽瑟姆在社交媒体上的视频消息中回应了司法部的事件，指责总统“出售”赦免并让他的同事受益。
纽瑟姆说：“对于今天与他站在一起的家人，你们的悲伤是真实的。这就是为什么加州前死囚牢房里的每一个人、每一个人都会死在监狱里。没有人走出监狱。唐纳德·特朗普的罪犯，他们走出监狱。”
“司法部起诉他的敌人并赦免他自己和他的朋友——这不是执法部门。这是保护费，”州长补充道。他此前在宣布他的计划时表示，“国家批准的杀戮与加州的价值观不相容。”
特朗普与遇难者家属握手，结束了这场悲痛的活动，其中一些人在几分钟前还流着泪。但当他离开舞台时，他的竞选歌曲——乐观的“基督教青年会”——响起时，基调很快发生了变化。
纽瑟姆和特朗普的争执发生在全国各地发生一系列拙劣的处决事件之际。上周，得克萨斯州监狱工作人员费力寻找雷纳尔多·丹尼斯身上的静脉，导致处决持续了一个多小时，丹尼斯痛苦地大喊大叫。 9 月，田纳西州死囚牢房中唯一的女性克里斯塔·派克 (Christa Pike) 成为第一个注射死刑的幸存者。她被安置在呼吸机上，几天后恢复了知觉。
自1994年高达80%以来，美国对死刑的支持率普遍下降，但美国人对死刑的感情却很复杂。
本月的盖洛普民意调查发现，49% 的美国成年人赞成对谋杀罪名成立的人判处死刑，45% 的人反对。但皮尤研究中心 8 月份的一项调查发现，66% 的美国人赞成对被判谋杀罪的人判处死刑，尽管 59% 的人表示死刑并不能威慑犯罪。此外还存在党派分歧，民主党人越来越反对死刑。
拉克尔·科罗内尔·乌里韦 (Raquel Coronell Uribe) 是 NBC 新闻的政治记者。

title_en: 2028 Democrats say Nvidia news is another example of corruption in government
title_zh: 2028 民主党人称英伟达新闻是政府腐败的另一个例子
summary: Potential Democratic presidential candidates are slamming the reinstatement of Nvidia’s CEO by leaning into a theme that carried them through the midterms.
summary_zh: 潜在的民主党总统候选人通过倾向于支持他们度过中期的主题来猛烈抨击英伟达首席执行官的复职
body_en: Democrats weighing 2028 presidential bids are using Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia as another opportunity to accuse the White House of corruption.
It’s a message that appeared to work well for them earlier this month: Voters resoundingly rejected President Donald Trump’s agenda, angry over high prices and an economy that benefited a select few.
Now, Democrats are keen to repeat that core political argument — especially after Trump took credit for helping reinstate Huang.
“This is the greed and lack of accountability that the country just rejected,” Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker said in a statement .

“The sheer corruption and weakness of Donald Trump is hurting America and putting our economy and national security at risk,” Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro wrote in a statement , describing Huang’s reinstatement is an example of “a rigged system that protects those at the very top.”

Former Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel told Decoded by POLITICO: “The number one rule is that the rule of law will hold the banker, the billionaire, and the baker to the same standard,” he said. “Now you tell me: What’s good about capitalism when you have a president of the United States pressing a public board to reverse themselves on their own governance? What is good about that decision?”

Pritzker, Shapiro and Emanuel are among the wide field of prospective Democratic presidential candidates. Their immediate decision to criticize Huang’s return as head of the massive chip company puts them at odds with top Silicon Valley leaders , including Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, who had called for Huang to be reinstated after he stepped down.

The public statements also show that these top Democrats are holding onto the playbook that campaigns used to dominate in the midterm elections, when the party firmly regained control of the House, Senate and statehouses around the country.

Earlier this month, Huang resigned from his role as CEO of Nvidia after he reportedly had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy and two company employees . On Monday, he was reinstated by a unanimous board vote after Trump publicly called for his return and pushed for it with board members over the weekend.

Huang’s close relationship with Trump has come under scrutiny since news of his affairs broke. The two spoke frequently, with Trump even calling Huang directly while he was on stage at a tech conference. The New York Times previously reported that Trump and top administration officials were aware that Huang was in a relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy — but chose not to act.
And Trump critics from both parties have pointed to Nvidia’s $25 million donation to the president’s White House ballroom project under Huang’s leadership as an example of Trump’s alleged corruption.

In a statement, the White House said that “today’s decision by Nvidia will preserve America’s technological edge over China, strengthen our national security, and ensure the future of SI continues to be built in America.”

“The Huang situation at its core is about corruption,” Republican former New Jersey Gov. Chris Christie, who is considering another presidential bid , said last week, referencing the ballroom donation. “So when something came up that was serious, what happened? Trump walked away from it and wouldn’t deal with it. That’s the intersection of corruption and incompetence that causes the American people to lose.”
Maryland Democratic Gov. Wes Moore, who also is considering a bid, told Axios the move from Huang amounted to a double standard for Trump’s allies and the rest of America.

"It seems like it's rules for me, but not for thee,” he said. “You have the wealthy and the powerful and the well-connected that are now making decisions to reinstate where, frankly, if that was any of us we would be held to a different type of standard.”
That messaging could continue to prove effective.

During the midterms, Democratic groups zeroed in on corruption in the White House and sought to connect high gas and grocery prices to a Trump administration they said flouted basic ethical rules while protecting and enriching powerful allies of the president. They connected corruption to the Epstein files, data centers , stock trading and other topics, reinforcing that unscrupulous dealings were at play while costs were going up.

Polling obtained by POLITICO in the weeks leading up to Election Day shows the vast majority of Americans — both Democrats and Republicans — say corruption is driving up their costs. And a September poll from Gallup also found about 90 percent of Americans believe corruption is rampant in government.

Democrats and several Republicans on Capitol Hill are pushing for more transparency on the extent to which Nvidia’s chips ended up in Chinese hands and further details on Huang’s relationship with suspected spy Alice Huang.

“Today's news that Donald Trump engineered the rehiring of Jensen Huang at Nvidia is Exhibit A about the political corruption and rot at the heart of the Trump administration's big tech and AI policy,” Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen, who is running to lead Senate Democrats, said in a briefing to reporters. Van Hollen was speculated as a possible 2028 presidential candidate, though he’s now ruled out a White House bid.
body_zh: 正在考虑 2028 年总统竞选的民主党人利用黄仁勋重返英伟达作为指责白宫腐败的另一个机会。
本月早些时候，这个信息似乎对他们很有效：选民坚决拒绝了唐纳德·特朗普总统的议程，对高物价和有利于少数人的经济感到愤怒。
现在，民主党人热衷于重复这一核心政治论点——尤其是在特朗普因帮助黄仁勋复职而获得赞誉之后。
伊利诺伊州州长 JB Pritzker 在一份声明中表示：“这个国家刚刚拒绝了这种贪婪和缺乏责任感。”
宾夕法尼亚州州长乔什·夏皮罗在一份声明中写道：“唐纳德·特朗普的纯粹腐败和软弱正在伤害美国，并使我们的经济和国家安全面临风险。”他将黄的复职描述为“保护最高层人士的被操纵制度”的一个例子。
前芝加哥市长拉姆·伊曼纽尔 (Rahm Emanuel) 告诉《政治解码》(Decoded by POLITICO)：“首要规则是法治将使银行家、亿万富翁和面包师遵守相同的标准，”他说。 “现在你告诉我：当美国总统迫使公共董事会改变自己的治理时，资本主义有什么好处？这个决定有什么好处？”
普利兹克、夏皮罗和伊曼纽尔都是潜在的民主党总统候选人。他们立即决定批评黄仁勋重新担任这家大型芯片公司的负责人，这让他们与硅谷高层领导人产生了分歧，其中包括特斯拉和 SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk)，后者曾呼吁黄仁勋下台后复职。
公开声明还表明，这些民主党高层仍在坚持竞选活动在中期选举中占据主导地位的策略，当时该党牢牢地重新控制了众议院、参议院和全国各地的州议会。
本月早些时候，黄仁勋辞去英伟达首席执行官一职，此前有报道称他与一名疑似中国间谍和两名公司员工有染。周一，在特朗普公开呼吁他回归并在周末与董事会成员推动后，董事会一致投票恢复了他的职位。
自从黄的绯闻曝光以来，他与特朗普的密切关系就受到了密切关注。两人经常交谈，特朗普甚至在黄在科技会议舞台上时直接给他打电话。 《纽约时报》此前报道称，特朗普和政府高级官员知道黄与一名据信是中国间谍的女性有关系，但选择不采取行动。
来自两党的特朗普批评者都指出，英伟达向黄仁勋领导下的总统白宫宴会厅项目捐赠了 2500 万美元，作为特朗普涉嫌腐败的一个例子。
白宫在一份声明中表示，“英伟达今天的决定将保持美国相对于中国的技术优势，加强我们的国家安全，并确保 SI 的未来继续在美国建设。”
“黄的情况的核心是腐败，”正在考虑再次竞选总统的共和党前新泽西州州长克里斯·克里斯蒂上周在提到舞厅捐款时表示。 “那么，当出现严重问题时，发生了什么？特朗普就走开，不去处理它。这就是腐败和无能的交叉点，导致美国人民蒙受损失。”
马里兰州民主党州长韦斯·摩尔也在考虑竞选，他告诉 Axios，黄的举动对特朗普的盟友和美国其他国家来说是双重标准。
“看起来这对我来说是规则，但对你来说不是，”他说。 “有钱有势、人脉广泛的人现在正在做出恢复的决定，坦率地说，如果是我们中的任何一个人，我们都会被要求遵守不同类型的标准。”
这种信息可能会继续有效。
在中期选举期间，民主党团体将矛头指向白宫的腐败问题，并试图将高油价和食品杂货价格与特朗普政府联系起来，他们称特朗普政府藐视基本道德规则，同时保护和致富了总统的强大盟友。他们将腐败与爱泼斯坦档案、数据中心、股票交易和其他话题联系起来，强调在成本上涨的同时，不道德的交易正在发挥作用。
《政治》杂志在选举日前几周获得的民意调查显示，绝大多数美国人——无论是民主党人还是共和党人——都表示腐败正在推高他们的成本。盖洛普 9 月份的一项民意调查还发现，约 90% 的美国人认为政府腐败猖獗。
国会山的民主党人和几位共和党人正在推动提高英伟达芯片最终落入中国人手中的程度的透明度，以及黄与可疑间谍黄爱丽丝关系的更多细节。

正在竞选参议院民主党领袖的马里兰州参议员克里斯·范·霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen) 在向记者举行的简报中表示，“今天的新闻是唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 策划重新聘用英伟达 (Nvidia) 黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang)，这就是特朗普政府大型科技和人工智能政策核心的政治腐败和腐败的证据。”范霍伦被猜测可能是 2028 年总统候选人，不过他现在已经排除了竞选白宫的可能性。

title_en: California Democrat Rep. Gomez resigns following ethics report on sexual misconduct allegations
title_zh: 加州民主党众议员戈麦斯在有关不当性行为指控的道德报告后辞职
summary: California Congressman Rep. Jimmy Gomez says he will resign after a House Ethics report concluded Gomez's actions violated House rules by "making unwelcome sexual advances."
summary_zh: 加利福尼亚州众议员吉米·戈麦斯表示，在众议院道德报告得出戈麦斯的行为违反了众议院规则后，他将辞职。
body_en: U.S. Rep. Jimmy Gomez, seen here at a Congressional hearing in March, announced Monday that he would resign following a report from the House Ethics committee on allegations of sexual misconduct. Heather Diehl/Getty Images North America hide caption
Rep. Jimmy Gomez, D-Calif., says he is resigning from Congress after a bipartisan investigation released Monday found "substantial evidence" he engaged in sexual misconduct toward a House staffer.

The House Ethics Committee concluded Gomez violated House rules by "making unwelcome sexual advances and engaging in unwelcome sexual conduct towards a House staffer and disregarding the power imbalance inherent in his relationship with House staffers."
The report also says the behavior could constitute criminal sexual assault.

Gomez has served in Congress since 2017 representing parts of Los Angeles. He lost reelection this fall to fellow Democrat Angela Gonzales-Torres. California uses a system where the top two vote-getters no matter the party advance to the general election. Gomez says his resignation will be effective Dec. 1.
Lisa Banks and Sarah Nesbitt, attorneys for the unnamed House staffer, wrote in a statement that their client testified to the committee truthfully and at personal risk.

"She sacrificed her own sense of safety and privacy to help reveal the ongoing misogyny and debauchery that permeates Capitol Hill," Banks and Nesbitt wrote. "Representative Gomez seems to believe that the power he wields, both as a man and as a member of Congress, makes him untouchable. Today's findings are a meaningful step toward dismantling that belief."
In a statement announcing his plan to resign, Gomez wrote that he cooperated with the investigation, but has strong disagreements with the report and its conclusions.
"Among other significant deficiencies and omissions, the report does not include key portions of my testimony that are essential to a full and fair understanding of what occurred," he wrote.

"I also have serious concerns about the process. In my interview, I answered the Committee's questions only to see my statements selectively quoted, disparaged, and disregarded throughout the final report, to which I was given no opportunity to respond."
Democratic Rep. Jimmy Gomez being investigated over sexual misconduct allegations

The House Ethics Committee, which includes five Democrats and five Republicans, opened its investigation into Gomez in August following a press report of Gomez kissing a staffer from another Congressional office at a party. Gomez denied those allegations.

The committee asked Gomez to disclose whether he "ever engaged in a romantic or sexual relationship or made sexual contact with a congressional staffer." Gomez disclosed interactions with two women — telling the committee the encounters were all consensual. Both women spoke to the committee.

One denied "she had ever had a nonconsensual sexual encounter" with Gomez. The other, described as Witness 1 in the report, said she had more than one encounter with Gomez and she did not consider them consensual.
She told investigators that Gomez made sexual contact without her consent at a bar in February 2024 and then was forceful with her and tried to kiss her at his congressional office in July 2024.
Gomez denied the interactions were nonconsensual. The staffer, described as Witness 1 in the committee report, eventually left her job on Capitol Hill.

"Here, the House lost Witness 1 as a competent and able staffer because of Representative Gomez's misconduct and because of a broader culture of disrespect and toxic sexual behavior toward staff that permeates life on the Hill and is long overdue for correction," the committee wrote.
The report comes amid a broader conversation about how Congress deals with the behavior of its members, especially when it comes to sexual misconduct.

In April, Democrat Eric Swalwell of California resigned his House seat amid allegations of sexual assault and misconduct. He also denied the allegations. Rep. Tony Gonzales (R-Tex.) also resigned from the House after admitting to an affair with a former staff member.
body_zh: 美国众议员吉米·戈麦斯 (Jimmy Gomez) 在 3 月份出席国会听证会时宣布，在众议院道德委员会就不当性行为指控提出报告后，他将辞职。希瑟·迪尔/盖蒂图片社北美隐藏标题栏
加利福尼亚州民主党众议员吉米·戈麦斯表示，在周一公布的两党调查发现“大量证据”表明他对众议院工作人员有不当性行为后，他将辞去国会职务。
众议院道德委员会得出结论，戈麦斯违反了众议院规则，“对众议院工作人员进行不受欢迎的性挑衅和从事不受欢迎的性行为，并且无视他与众议院工作人员关系中固有的权力不平衡。”
报告还称，这种行为可能构成刑事性侵犯。
戈麦斯自 2017 年以来一直代表洛杉矶部分地区在国会任职。今年秋天，他在连任中输给了民主党同僚安吉拉·冈萨雷斯-托雷斯。加州采用的制度是，无论哪个政党，得票最多的两名候选人都会进入大选。戈麦斯表示，他的辞职将于 12 月 1 日生效。
这名未透露姓名的众议院工作人员的律师丽莎·班克斯和莎拉·内斯比特在一份声明中写道，他们的当事人如实向委员会作证，并承担个人风险。
班克斯和内斯比特写道：“她牺牲了自己的安全感和隐私感，以帮助揭露国会山持续存在的厌女症和放荡行为。” “戈麦斯众议员似乎相信，他所拥有的权力，无论是作为一个男人还是作为一名国会议员，都使他不可动摇。今天的调查结果是朝着消除这种信念迈出的有意义的一步。”
戈麦斯在一份宣布计划辞职的声明中写道，他配合了调查，但对报告及其结论有强烈分歧。
他写道：“除了其他重大缺陷和遗漏之外，该报告没有包括我证词的关键部分，而这些部分对于全面、公正地理解所发生的事情至关重要。”
“我也对这一过程感到严重关切。在采访中，我回答了委员会的问题，却发现我的陈述在整个最终报告中被选择性地引用、贬低和忽视，而我没有机会对此做出回应。”
民主党众议员吉米·戈麦斯因性行为不端指控接受调查
包括五名民主党人和五名共和党人在内的众议院道德委员会于八月开始对戈麦斯进行调查，此前有媒体报道称戈麦斯在一次聚会上亲吻了另一国会办公室的一名工作人员。戈麦斯否认了这些指控。
该委员会要求戈麦斯披露他是否“曾经与国会工作人员发生过恋爱关系或性关系，或者有过性接触”。戈麦斯披露了与两名女性的互动——告诉委员会，这些接触都是双方自愿的。两位女士都向委员会发表了讲话。
其中一人否认“她曾与戈麦斯发生过非自愿的性行为”。另一位在报告中被称为“目击者 1”的人表示，她与戈麦斯不止一次相遇，但她并不认为他们是自愿的。
她告诉调查人员，戈麦斯于 2024 年 2 月在一家酒吧未经她同意进行了性接触，然后于 2024 年 7 月在他的国会办公室对她使用暴力并试图亲吻她。
戈麦斯否认这些互动是非自愿的。委员会报告中将这名工作人员称为“目击者 1”，她最终辞去了国会山的工作。
委员会写道：“众议院失去了证人一号，因为众议员戈麦斯的不当行为，以及对工作人员的不尊重和有毒性行为的更广泛文化，这种文化渗透到了国会的生活中，早就应该得到纠正。”
该报告发布之际，人们正在就国会如何处理其成员的行为，尤其是不当性行为进行更广泛的讨论。
四月，加利福尼亚州民主党人埃里克·斯瓦尔韦尔因性侵犯和不当行为指控而辞去了众议院席位。他还否认了这些指控。众议员托尼·冈萨雷斯（德克萨斯州共和党人）在承认与一名前工作人员有染后也辞去众议院职务。

title_en: Jimmy Gomez to resign after House ethics panel finds evidence of sexual misconduct
title_zh: 众议院道德小组发现不当性行为证据后吉米·戈麦斯辞职
summary: Democrat, who lost re-election bid, found to have made ‘unwelcome sexual advances’ towards House staffer Jimmy Gomez will resign from Congress after a House ethics report released on Monday found “substantial evidence” that the California Democrat had “engaged
summary_zh: 连任竞选失败的民主党人被发现对众议院工作人员吉米·戈麦斯进行了“不受欢迎的性挑衅”，之后将辞去国会职务。
body_en: Democrat, who lost re-election bid, found to have made ‘unwelcome sexual advances’ towards House staffer

Jimmy Gomez will resign from Congress after a House ethics report released on Monday found “substantial evidence” that the California Democrat had “engaged in sexual misconduct”, including by “making unwelcome sexual advances and sexual contact toward a House staffer”.

The 19-page report from the House ethics committee found that Gomez “made unwanted sexual advances” toward a House staffer on two occasions, “including an incident in which he made sexual contact with her and another in which he was ‘forceful’ with her in his congressional office”.
Gomez, who represents parts of Los Angeles, lost his re-election bid earlier this month to the democratic socialist Angela Gonzales-Torres and was set to leave Congress in January.
Following the publication of the report, Gomez announced he would resign on 1 December.

The congressman said that he had “strong disagreements with the committee’s report and its conclusions” but said he took full responsibility for the “personal mistakes I committed outside of my marriage”.
Gomez said he cooperated with the investigation and responded voluntarily to requests for information.
In a joint statement, House Democratic leaders called the report “serious and deeply troubling”.

“It is appropriate that he is stepping down. Decisive action to set a new standard for reform is an urgent priority for House Democrats ,” Representatives Hakeem Jeffries, Katherine Clark and Pete Aguilar, who are expected to serve as House speaker, majority leader and majority whip in January, said.

“We strongly support the effort led by Teresa Leger Fernández and the Democratic women’s caucus to reform the House rules in order to protect members and staff from instances of sexual harassment and misconduct. It’s time to rebuild trust in the institution.”
The report stated that “Gomez’s conduct also reflects a broader environment of sexual misconduct and toxic working conditions in some Capitol Hill offices”.
The allegations against Gomez are the latest in a series of ethics investigations that have seen a slew of representatives resign from Congress or lose their bids for re-election this year.

In April, Eric Swalwell, also a Democratic representative from California, resigned from Congress following multiple allegations of sexual assault and misconduct that ended his bid for governor and saw a dramatic reshuffling in the race. Gomez was a co-chair of Swalwell’s gubernatorial campaign and stepped down after the allegations against Swalwell were made public.
That same month, Tony Gonzales, a Texas Republican, stepped down after admitting that he had an affair with an aide who later died by suicide.

In August, the Republican congressman Chuck Edwards, of North Carolina, announced he would not run for re-election after an ethics committee report determined that he “fostered a hostile work environment and engaged in sexual harassment” by giving gifts and lavishing attention on two young female staffers.

Cory Mills, a Florida Republican who is accused of a variety of ethical lapses, was defeated in the Republican primary. In October 2025, a Florida judge granted a protective order against Mills at the request of his former girlfriend.

In November’s midterm elections, Max Miller, a Republican from Ohio, lost his bid for re-election amid a House ethics investigation into drug use and domestic abuse allegations surrounding his divorce to Emily Moreno, the daughter Bernie Moreno, a Republican US senator.
The House ethics report on Gomez did not make any specific recommendations.
It noted: “The constitution charges the House with policing the behavior of its own members, and the House should take whatever action it deems appropriate in light of the committee’s findings.”
body_zh: 竞选连任失败的民主党人被发现对众议院工作人员进行了“不受欢迎的性挑衅”
周一发布的众议院道德报告发现“大量证据”表明这位加州民主党人“从事不当性行为”，包括“对众议院工作人员进行不受欢迎的性挑逗和性接触”，吉米·戈麦斯将从国会辞职。
众议院道德委员会这份长达19页的报告发现，戈麦斯曾两次对众议院工作人员“做出不受欢迎的性侵犯”，“其中一次是他与她发生性接触，另一次是他在国会办公室对她‘强行’”。
代表洛杉矶部分地区的戈麦斯本月早些时候在连任竞选中输给了民主社会主义者安吉拉·冈萨雷斯-托雷斯，并计划于一月份离开国会。
报告发表后，戈麦斯宣布将于 12 月 1 日辞职。
这位国会议员表示，他“强烈反对委员会的报告及其结论”，但表示他对“我在婚姻之外犯下的个人错误”承担全部责任。
戈麦斯表示，他配合调查并自愿回应信息请求。
众议院民主党领导人在一份联合声明中称该报告“严重且令人深感不安”。
“他辞职是适当的。采取果断行动制定新的改革标准是众议院民主党人的当务之急，”预计将在一月份担任众议院议长、多数党领袖和多数党鞭的众议员哈基姆·杰弗里斯、凯瑟琳·克拉克和皮特·阿吉拉尔表示。
“我们强烈支持特雷莎·莱杰·费尔南德斯和民主党妇女核心小组领导的改革众议院规则的努力，以保护议员和工作人员免受性骚扰和不当行为的侵害。现在是重建对该机构的信任的时候了。”
报告指出，“戈麦斯的行为也反映了国会山一些办公室更广泛的不当性行为和有毒工作条件”。
针对戈麦斯的指控是一系列道德调查中的最新一起，在这些调查中，许多代表辞去了国会职务或失去了今年的连任竞选。
今年 4 月，来自加利福尼亚州的民主党众议员埃里克·斯瓦尔韦尔 (Eric Swalwell) 在受到多项性侵犯和不当行为指控后辞去了国会职务，这导致他竞选州长的努力结束，竞选也出现了戏剧性的改组。戈麦斯是斯瓦尔韦尔州长竞选的联合主席，在对斯瓦尔韦尔的指控公开后辞职。
同月，得克萨斯州共和党人托尼·冈萨雷斯在承认自己与一名助手有染后辞职，该助手后来自杀身亡。
八月，北卡罗来纳州共和党众议员查克·爱德华兹 (Chuck Edwards) 宣布，在一份道德委员会报告认定他向两名年轻女职员赠送礼物和过度关注，“营造了敌对的工作环境并进行了性骚扰”后，他宣布不会竞选连任。
佛罗里达州共和党人科里·米尔斯 (Cory Mills) 在共和党初选中落败，他被指控犯有各种道德失误。 2025年10月，佛罗里达州一名法官应米尔斯前女友的请求，对他发出了保护令。
在 11 月的中期选举中，来自俄亥俄州的共和党人马克斯·米勒 (Max Miller) 因与美国共和党参议员伯尼·莫雷诺 (Bernie Moreno) 的女儿艾米丽·莫雷诺 (Emily Moreno) 离婚的吸毒和家庭虐待指控而受到众议院道德调查，因此失去了连任竞选。
众议院关于戈麦斯的道德报告没有提出任何具体建议。
它指出：“宪法责成众议院监管其议员的行为，众议院应根据委员会的调查结果采取其认为适当的任何行动。”

title_en: They attended Trump's controversial meme coin dinner. It didn't go well
title_zh: 他们参加了特朗普颇具争议的模因硬币晚宴。进展不顺利
summary: Trump held another meme coin dinner for top holders of his cryptocurrency — an event that has raised intense controversy. Here's an inside account from two guests who attended.
summary_zh: 特朗普为其加密货币的顶级持有者举办了另一场模因币晚宴，这一活动引起了激烈的争议。这是一个内部账户
body_en: They attended Trump’s controversial meme coin dinner. It didn’t go well Trump held another meme coin dinner for top holders of his cryptocurrency — an event that has raised intense controversy. Here's an inside account from two guests who attended.
Trump held another meme coin dinner for top holders of his cryptocurrency — an event that has raised intense controversy. Here's an inside account from two guests who attended.

With Democrats winning majorities in Congress, President Trump will likely face investigations into the billions of dollars he and his family have made in crypto. Despite that, the president held another dinner last night to reward the top holders of his meme coin, a cryptocurrency he launched right before his inauguration. NPR's Rafael Nam talked with two people who were there.

RAFAEL NAM, BYLINE: Crypto investor Morten Christensen was among the over a hundred guests who gathered at Trump's golf club on a damp evening in Northern Virginia. He was there to attend what was promoted as the most exclusive dinner in the world. He brought along his little sister. They rode together in an Uber.
MORTEN CHRISTENSEN: Yeah. I'm excited. It's always nice to dress up for an event. My sister looks amazing.

NAM: Christensen has attended these events before. This time, it was a lot less expensive. The coin has cratered in price. By using a sophisticated trading strategy, he says they were basically going for free. His sister, Gabrielle Felen, was decked out in a nice black dress.
GABRIELLE FELEN: Yeah. I'm also excited, a little bit nervous, but excited about how it's going to be.

NAM: Christensen and Felen have agreed to share voice memos through the night, and the three of us buckled in for the event. Trump's crypto events are controversial. The top holders of the coin get to spend time with the president. The more you buy, the closer the access. In the past, many of the attendees have not been from the U.S., raising concerns that Trump could be influenced, which the White House denies. Inside the swanky gala room, Christensen rattles off the people he's met.
CHRISTENSEN: One was from Saudi. One was from London. Met a couple of people from Ukraine, two people from India, four from China. I think one was from South Korea.

NAM: Christensen and Felen are also from abroad, from the Netherlands. They say it's not Trump's politics that drew them to the event. Christensen even believes meme coins are stupid, but it was a chance to see the leader of the free world up close and mingle with guests like Kevin O'Leary from "Shark Tank." But just as they got there, things started taking a turn. He thought he was on the VIP list.
CHRISTENSEN: I got into the entrance, and they said, I'm not on the VIP list, even though I have the email of VIP and everything, and they just said, I'm not on the list, so...

NAM: And just as they started getting ready for the president to walk in, a couple of people approached Christensen. He was getting kicked out for posting pictures online and talking to people in the media, like me. He ended up all the way outside the golf club in the middle of soaking rain.
CHRISTENSEN: So I got removed from the event, from the Trump gala. I'm not sure why.

NAM: NPR did not get a response from organizers as to why. At the golf course, they both decided Felen would stay. She had come all this way to see the president, and she finally got the moment she was waiting for.
UNIDENTIFIED MUSICAL ARTIST: (Singing) God bless the USA.
PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: Do you want to hear another one (ph)? Should we keep the song going?
NAM: Trump went on to deliver a speech that veered everywhere, from crypto to digs on Biden - a speech that Christensen never got to hear.
body_zh: 他们参加了特朗普颇具争议的模因硬币晚宴。特朗普为他的加密货币的顶级持有者举办了另一场模因币晚宴，这一活动引起了激烈的争议。这是两位出席嘉宾的内部叙述。
特朗普为其加密货币的顶级持有者举办了另一场模因币晚宴，这一活动引起了激烈的争议。这是两位出席嘉宾的内部叙述。
随着民主党在国会赢得多数席位，特朗普总统可能会面临对其及其家人在加密货币领域赚取的数十亿美元的调查。尽管如此，总统昨晚还是举行了另一场晚宴，以奖励他的模因币的顶级持有者，这是他在就职前夕推出的一种加密货币。 NPR 的拉斐尔·南 (Rafael Nam) 与在场的两个人进行了交谈。
拉斐尔·南连线：在北弗吉尼亚州一个潮湿的夜晚，加密货币投资者莫滕·克里斯滕森 (Morten Christensen) 是聚集在特朗普高尔夫俱乐部的一百多名客人之一。他在那里参加被宣传为世界上最独特的晚宴。他带着他的小妹妹一起来。他们一起乘坐优步。
莫滕·克里斯滕森：是的。我很兴奋。盛装出席活动总是好的。我姐姐看起来棒极了。
NAM：克里斯滕森以前参加过这些活动。这次，便宜了很多。硬币的价格已经下跌。他说，通过使用复杂的交易策略，他们基本上是免费的。他的妹妹加布里埃尔·费伦 (Gabrielle Felen) 穿着漂亮的黑色连衣裙。
加布里埃尔·费伦：是的。我也很兴奋，有点紧张，但对接下来的事情感到兴奋。
NAM：克里斯滕森和费伦同意整夜分享语音备忘录，我们三个人都全力以赴地参加了这次活动。特朗普的加密货币事件备受争议。硬币的最高持有者可以与总统共度时光。买得越多，获得的机会就越近。过去，许多与会者并非来自美国，这引发了人们对特朗普可能受到影响的担忧，但白宫否认了这一点。在豪华的宴会厅里，克里斯滕森滔滔不绝地讲述着他遇到的人。
克里斯滕森：其中一位来自沙特。一位来自伦敦。遇到了几个来自乌克兰的人，两个来自印度的人，四个来自中国的人。我认为其中一位来自韩国。
NAM：克里斯滕森和费伦也来自国外，来自荷兰。他们表示，吸引他们参加这次活动的并不是特朗普的政治观点。克里斯滕森甚至认为模因币很愚蠢，但这是一个近距离观察自由世界领袖并与《创智赢家》中的凯文·奥利里等嘉宾交流的机会。但就在他们到达那里时，事情开始发生转变。他以为自己在 VIP 名单上。
克里斯滕森：我走进入口，他们说，我不在 VIP 名单上，尽管我有 VIP 的电子邮件和一切，他们只是说，我不在名单上，所以......
南：正当他们开始准备总统走进来时，有几个人走近克里斯滕森。他因为在网上发布照片并与媒体上的人（比如我）交谈而被踢出局。他最终在大雨中一路走到高尔夫球俱乐部外面。
克里斯滕森：所以我被从活动中、从特朗普晚会上除名了。我不知道为什么。
NAM：NPR 没有得到组织者关于原因的回应。在高尔夫球场，他们都决定费伦留下来。她千里迢迢跑来见总统，终于等到了她等待的时刻。
身份不明的音乐艺术家：（唱歌）上帝保佑美国。
唐纳德·特朗普总统：你想再听听吗？我们应该继续唱这首歌吗？
NAM：特朗普接着发表了一场内容各异的演讲，从加密货币到挖苦拜登——克里斯滕森从未听过这场演讲。

title_en: Trump halts Iowa detonation, says new governor to blame if it blows accidentally
title_zh: 特朗普叫停爱荷华州爆炸，称如果意外爆炸，新州长应承担责任
summary: The Army said on Sunday that it would carry out the detonation on Wednesday.
summary_zh: 陆军周日表示，将于周三进行爆炸。
body_en: President Trump took to social media Monday afternoon to announce that he has ordered the US military to halt plans to detonate 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide at an Army ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa. Trump claimed that the fate of the unstable, highly explosive material is now in the hands of a federal court and Rob Sand, Iowa's governor-elect, who won't be sworn into office until January.

The Army had planned to detonate the barrels on November 20, but delayed the blast on Thursday amid public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups. The explosion will launch a plume of toxic gases and neurotoxic lead that could reach up to 100 miles away from the Iowa facility, the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP).

Iowa residents and officials said they learned of the detonation only days beforehand. The environmental groups, led by Earthjustice, claimed in an emergency court filing that the Army had not fully considered safer options for disposing of the lead azide before planning the detonation.
body_zh: 周一下午，特朗普总统在社交媒体上宣布，他已命令美军停止在爱荷华州米德尔敦一家陆军弹药厂引爆 68 桶劣质叠氮化铅的计划。特朗普声称，这种不稳定的高爆炸性材料的命运现在掌握在联邦法院和爱荷华州当选州长罗布·桑德的手中，后者要到一月份才会宣誓就职。
陆军原计划于 11 月 20 日引爆这些木桶，但由于公众强烈抗议和环保组织的法律挑战，推迟了周四的爆炸。爆炸将释放出大量有毒气体和神经毒性铅，这些气体和铅可能到达距离爱荷华州陆军弹药厂 (IAAAP) 100 英里的地方。
爱荷华州居民和官员表示，他们是在几天前才得知爆炸事件的。以地球正义组织为首的环保组织在一份紧急法庭文件中声称，陆军在计划爆炸之前没有充分考虑处理叠氮化铅的更安全的选择。

title_en: Republican senators criticize Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang
title_zh: 共和党参议员批评英伟达恢复黄仁勋的决定
summary: Outcry builds over Trump-backed move to bring back CEO as lawmakers call for Huang’s testimony before Congress US politics – live updates Republican lawmakers roundly criticized the Nvidia board’s decision to reinstate its chief executive, Jensen Huang, even a
summary_zh: 立法者呼吁黄在国会作证，特朗普支持召回首席执行官的举动引发强烈抗议 美国政治 - 共和党实时更新
body_en: Outcry builds over Trump-backed move to bring back CEO as lawmakers call for Huang’s testimony before Congress

Republican lawmakers roundly criticized the Nvidia board’s decision to reinstate its chief executive, Jensen Huang, even after Donald Trump said he spoke “directly and indirectly” with board members and “convinced them” to bring him back.
Pete Ricketts, a US senator from Nebraska, wrote on X that Huang’s “behavior does not support reinstatement”.
Ricketts, who sits on the Senate foreign relations committee, said Huang still needed to testify before Congress – and Nvidia still needed to answer questions about national security concerns.
John Curtis, a senator from Utah on the Senate commerce committee, noted that Nvidia’s board relied on information from government officials to reinstate Huang.

“Nvidia’s board says it relied on input from senior US officials to conclude that bringing Jensen Huang back posed no national security risk … Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board? And on what basis did the board conclude there was no risk?” Curtis asked .

John Cornyn, an outgoing senator from Texas, posted several times on social media, questioning whether the FBI conducted a defensive briefing on Huang, whether that information was ignored, Nvidia’s corporate governance, and more.
Tim Scott, the Republican senator for South Carolina who heads the Senate banking committee, set a date of 3 December for Huang to testify before the panel.
According to a notice sent by the committee, Huang is scheduled to be the only witness at the hearing, called “Protecting America’s AI Advantage: Oversight of US Export Controls” .
A chorus of Democrats joined with Republican criticizing Huang’s return to head the company.

Elizabeth Warren, a senator for Massachusetts who is likely to be the Senate banking chair when Democrats take control of the chamber in January, called the ​decision “reckless” and urged legislation to ensure stronger chip export controls.

“Jensen Huang’s return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan ⁠export control bills into law and making sure Nvidia does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at ​risk,” Warren said.
Warren’s call was echoed by the Senate Democratic leader, Chuck Schumer.
Hakeem Jeffries, ​the incoming speaker of the House, said that Congress should include “ironclad” legislation in the annual defense bill to prevent AI technology from reaching China.
The lawmakers’ comments came as Trump said on CNBC that he directly influenced the decision.

“I’ve been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it,” Trump said. “And I felt more strongly as I saw what was happening with the company, because that was, to me, a very important part of our country.”

Huang resigned from Nvidia earlier this month after reports of extramarital affairs including with a woman who US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy. When the chipmaker announced on Monday that he had been reinstated, Nvidia shares jumped 33%.
The president said in the CNBC phone interview that the company’s board asked for assurances on national security risks, which Trump said the administration gave them.
“They did ask for assurance on the national security threat,” the US president said. “And we gave him assurance at least with everything we know, and we know a lot.”
body_zh: 随着立法者要求黄在国会作证，特朗普支持的首席执行官召回行动引发强烈抗议
共和党议员严厉批评英伟达董事会恢复首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 职务的决定，尽管唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 表示，他“直接和间接”与董事会成员进行了交谈，并“说服了他们”让他回来。
来自内布拉斯加州的美国参议员皮特·里基茨(Pete Ricketts)在X上写道，黄的“行为不支持复职”。
参议院外交关系委员会成员里基茨表示，黄仁勋仍然需要在国会作证，而英伟达仍然需要回答有关国家安全问题的问题。
参议院商务委员会的犹他州参议员约翰·柯蒂斯 (John Curtis) 指出，英伟达董事会依靠政府官员的信息来恢复黄的职位。
“英伟达董事会表示，它根据美国高级官员的意见得出结论，让黄仁勋回来不会构成国家安全风险……我们政府中的谁参与了权衡？他们告诉了董事会什么？董事会基于什么基础得出不存在风险的结论？”柯蒂斯问道。
即将离任的德克萨斯州参议员约翰·科宁 (John Cornyn) 多次在社交媒体上发帖，质疑 FBI 是否对黄仁勋进行了防御性简报、这些信息是否被忽视、英伟达的公司治理等等。
参议院银行委员会主席、南卡罗来纳州共和党参议员蒂姆·斯科特 (Tim Scott) 定下黄在 12 月 3 日在专家组作证的日期。
根据该委员会发出的通知，黄计划将成为听证会的唯一证人，该听证会名为“保护美国的人工智能优势：美国出口管制的监督”。
民主党人和共和党人齐声批评黄重返公司领导。
马萨诸塞州参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦 (Elizabeth Warren) 称这一决定“鲁莽”，并敦促立法确保加强芯片出口管制。她很可能在民主党一月份控制参议院时担任参议院银行业主席。
沃伦表示：“黄仁勋的回归只会增加将两党出口管制法案通过为法律的紧迫性，并确保英伟达不会游说废除该立法并使我们的国家安全面临风险。”
沃伦的呼吁得到了参议院民主党领袖查克·舒默的响应。
即将上任的众议院议长哈基姆·杰弗里斯 (Hakeem Jeffries) 表示，国会应在年度国防法案中纳入“铁定”立法，以防止人工智能技术进入中国。
议员们发表评论之际，特朗普在 CNBC 上表示，他直接影响了这一决定。
特朗普表示：“我一直在直接和间接地与董事会交谈，对此我的感受非常强烈。” “当我看到公司发生的事情时，我的感受更加强烈，因为对我来说，这是我们国家非常重要的一部分。”
本月早些时候，黄仁勋因婚外情报道而从英伟达辞职，其中包括与美国情报部门认为是中国间谍的一名女性的婚外情。当这家芯片制造商周一宣布他已复职时，英伟达股价上涨了 33%。
总统在接受 CNBC 电话采访时表示，该公司董事会要求就国家安全风险做出保证，特朗普称政府已向他们提供了保证。
美国总统表示：“他们确实要求就国家安全威胁做出保证。” “我们至少用我们所知道的一切向他保证，而且我们知道很多。”

summary: High costs during Chad Bianco’s failed run for governor, including a $665 steak dinner, have raised concerns A southern California county spent more than $3m in a year on a security detail for its sheriff, Chad Bianco, a former Republican candidate for governo
summary_zh: 查德·比安科 (Chad Bianco) 竞选州长失败期间的高昂费用，包括 665 美元的牛排晚餐，引发了人们的担忧。
body_en: Republican sheriff racked up $3m security bill for California taxpayers, including Ritz-Carlton stays and steak | California
High costs during Chad Bianco’s failed run for governor, including a $665 steak dinner, have raised concerns

A southern California county spent more than $3m in a year on a security detail for its sheriff, Chad Bianco, a former Republican candidate for governor, and taxpayers footed the bill for items such as hotels rooms, travel and a $665 steak dinner.

A report from the Riverside county auditor-controller showed costs surged during the final months of Bianco’s gubernatorial campaign, peaking at $439,000 in April, and included flights, hotels, rental cars and meals for security personnel for campaign events.

The transactions cited in the report, which was first covered by the Riverside Press-Enterprise , include rooms at the Ritz Carlton in St Louis, where Bianco appeared on a podcast and a steak dinner in Los Angeles.
The high costs, including to support Bianco during his unsuccessful campaign, have raised concerns in the county.
“That amount of money spent in a given year is troubling,” Jose Medina, a county supervisor, told the Riverside Record . “It seems to be quite a very high figure.”

The sheriff’s office has pushed back against Medina’s criticism, arguing that the expenditures were necessary because of the death threats the sheriff had received. Don Sharp, the county undersheriff and Bianco’s chief of staff, said he was behind the decision to form and deploy the security detail.
Bianco’s “position, public visibility and the nature of the threats directed toward him create security concerns that extend beyond the walls” of his workplace, Sharp said in a statement.

“The security measures in place are based on safety considerations, not political disagreements. It is unfortunate that the need to protect an elected official has become a subject of political criticism,” Sharp said, adding that Medina “has repeatedly demonstrated his opposition to the sheriff”.
“Disagreements over policy and politics should never overshadow the fundamental responsibility to take threats against public officials seriously.”

Sharp also said that Bianco began receiving death threats during the pandemic, during which time he expressed opposition to state public health mandates, and that those threats “intensified over time, resulting in arrests both in California and out of state”.

Bianco came into the national spotlight in late 2020 when he criticized the approach of the California governor, Gavin Newsom, to Covid, and his “dictatorial attitude” toward Californians. He encouraged people to mask and practice social distancing, but called business closures and stay-at-home orders “ridiculous”.
He endorsed Donald Trump in 2024, stating : “I think it’s time to put a felon in the White House.”
In 2025, Bianco announced he would run for California governor as a Republican. During the primary, he came fourth and failed to advance to the general election.

This year Bianco also drew attention when he confiscated 650,000 ballots as part of an inquiry into specious allegations of fraud, an unprecedented move that the state supreme court determined violated election law. He was ordered to return the ballots.
Security costs began declining in June, before rising to $283,000 in September. In October, costs fell to $87,000 for the month.
